channel.title: Tobias Deekens - Blogroll
channel.description: A collection of blog posts I enjoyed reading and found worth sharing.

item.title: A Technical Deep Dive Into the New Raycast
item.author: Raycast
item.description: A hybrid architecture pairing native shells with React shows web technology can deliver desktop feel without Chromium bloat. Cross-platform parity came from intentional choices about feel, not framework selection.

item.title: The Last Six Months in LLMs in Five Minutes
item.author: Simon Willison
item.description: Coding agents crossed into production-ready reliability while open-weight models exceeded expectations on consumer hardware. Model leadership shifted across providers five times in six months.

item.title: How to Avoid AI Code Slop
item.author: Eng Leadership
item.description: AI-generated code passes the eye test while hiding subtle logical errors. Documenting intent before generation and automating surface checks catches design issues earlier than waiting on code review to find them.

item.title: AI Is Too Expensive
item.author: Ed Zitron
item.description: Hyperscalers burned hundreds of billions on AI infrastructure without a clear path to profitability. Enterprise spend lacks measurable ROI, exposing the gap between executive narrative and what the unit economics actually support.

item.title: Prosocial Contagion
item.author: Andi Roberts
item.description: Individual actions propagate through social networks up to three degrees of separation. Modeling citizenship through visible behavior shifts organizational norms more reliably than any policy mandate.

item.title: Claude Is Not Your Architect
item.author: Holland Tech
item.description: AI agents are strong implementers but lack accountability and contextual judgment for the decisions that actually matter. Human debate about constraints and trade-offs still produces better architecture than deferring to confident but ungrounded machine output.

item.title: Year in Open Source
item.author: rman.dev
item.description: Consistent contribution and visible work in open source accelerates growth past traditional career paths. Communication and community engagement earn recognition and responsibility faster than corporate ladders measure them.

item.title: Not So Locked In Anymore
item.author: Simon Willison
item.description: Coding agents drop the cost of porting between languages, turning stack choices from permanent lock-in into manageable technical debt. Bun's Zig to Rust migration hints at how fluid these decisions become.

item.title: Apple Silicon Costs More Than OpenRouter
item.author: William Angel
item.description: Local LLM inference on Apple Silicon costs roughly 3x more per token than cloud providers once hardware depreciation is included. Speed and privacy, not raw cost, are what justify keeping inference on the machine.

item.title: GitLab Act 2
item.author: GitLab
item.description: GitLab restructures around five architectural bets and flattens hierarchies to position itself for machine-directed development. The premise is that agentic software construction requires fundamental platform redesign, not AI bolted on the side.

item.title: LLMs Are Functions, Not Brains
item.author: James Pritchard
item.description: Treating language models as autonomous agents adds latency and unpredictability. Typed input-output functions enable testability, composability, and debugging at lower cost than agentic workflows trying to reason their way to the same result.

item.title: The Anatomy of an AI-Native Org
item.author: Ajey Gore
item.description: AI collapses the translation layer between strategy and execution, eating most middle-management coordination. The 'what' expands while the 'how' shrinks, leaving judgment-heavy engineering and product roles as the only ones that scale.

item.title: The Science of Social Loafing
item.author: Corporate Rebels
item.description: Group effort drops predictably as team size grows, an effect Ringelmann measured a century ago. Small autonomous units, radical transparency, and peer accountability counter it better than adding hierarchical oversight.

item.title: How to Finish Engineering Projects Early Without Added Stress
item.author: Eng Leadership
item.description: Critical chain pools task buffers at the project level instead of padding individual estimates. Cutting estimates in half and tracking buffer consumption against progress surfaces scope creep weeks earlier than burndown charts.

item.title: Fix Delivery First
item.author: Ant Murphy
item.description: Discovery, OKRs, and AI rarely help a struggling product org until delivery works. Slow release cycles and accumulated tech debt are the actual bottleneck, and everything strategic downstream treats symptoms instead of cause.

item.title: The Design System Advantage Is Memory
item.author: The Design System Guide
item.description: Design system value lives in accessible organizational memory, not in the tooling. Agents make confident mistakes when decision history scatters across Slack and ADRs. Structure data and governance first, then layer orchestration on top.

item.title: You Taught the Company to Overload You
item.author: Aviv Ben-Yosef
item.description: Leaders who always say yes erase their own judgment and train the organization to keep demanding more. Making commitment costs visible and holding operational boundaries breaks the loop before it becomes the role.

item.title: Migrating from Go to Rust
item.author: corrode
item.description: Go validates at runtime through discipline and tools. Rust encodes correctness into compile-time types that prevent entire categories of bugs. The trade is steeper upfront complexity for dramatically fewer production incidents.

item.title: Maintainability Sensors for Coding Agents
item.author: Martin Fowler
item.description: Coding agents produce better code when given real-time feedback loops like linting, dependency rules, and mutation testing. Computational analysis catches mechanics; semantic issues across files still need LLM interpretation to surface.

item.title: State of the Software Engineering Job Market in 2026
item.author: Gergely Orosz
item.description: Tech hiring growth diverges by geography. The US and UK expanded while Germany and France contracted. AI engineering roles surged 50 to 100% at major firms, outpacing general software engineer recruitment.

item.title: AI-Assisted Engineers Are Burning Out
item.author: Evil Martians
item.description: Code generation compresses work into shorter timeframes but concentrates cognitive load, replacing craft satisfaction with reviews and iteration. More output ships, less fulfillment remains, and burnout follows the density of thinking, not the hours.

item.title: Exception, Presence, Delegation
item.author: John Cutler
item.description: Three management motions form one system. Exceptions flag deviations, presence transfers tacit knowledge, delegation pushes authority to local expertise. Run any of them alone and you get dashboards no one reads or leaders trapped in every meeting.

item.title: Is AI Causing a Repeat of Frontend's Lost Decade?
item.author: Mastro
item.description: AI abstracts away manual coding the way frameworks abstracted browser mechanics, lowering both skill requirements and worker leverage. Leaky abstractions resurface when the tooling fails, and understanding the layer below stays non-negotiable.

item.title: The State of CSS Centering in 2026
item.author: CSS-Tricks
item.description: Centering looks simple but demands different analysis across Flexbox, Grid, and positioning. Modern properties like text-box and anchor-center finally close the historical precision gaps that older recipes papered over.

item.title: You Need AI That Reduces Maintenance Costs
item.author: James Shore
item.description: Productivity gains turn into permanent indenture if maintenance cost rises with output. Doubling code volume without halving its long-term cost leaves teams trapped under their own velocity.

item.title: Why Senior Developers Fail to Communicate Their Expertise
item.author: Nair
item.description: Seniors talk in complexity while the business talks in uncertainty. Reframing expertise as a solution to speed problems shifts seniors from objectors into editors of rapid AI-generated output.

item.title: Open Source Resistance
item.author: Open Source Resistance
item.description: Maintainers should treat OSS work on company time as legitimate professional work, not a side hustle. A direct-action stance on balancing corporate value extraction with maintainer sustainability.

item.title: How I Moved My Digital Stack to Europe
item.author: Monokai
item.description: European infrastructure providers run at production quality for most workloads. A two-month migration shows sovereignty is feasible; keep US services only where the context-specific advantage outweighs the cost.

item.title: Agile in the Age of AI
item.author: Miren
item.description: AI authors code at scale while humans shift to editor and director. The constraint is not technology but the human cognitive ceiling and the 24/7 pressure that erodes Agile's core principle.

item.title: Common Engineering Strategy Failure Factors
item.author: Aleix Morgadas
item.description: Technical decisions dominate engineering strategy while human alignment, communication, and realistic planning get skipped. Execution lives in those overlooked organizational factors, not the architecture diagram.

item.title: Being Strategic: What That Actually Means
item.author: J. Gefroh
item.description: Strategic thinking is a teachable progression of analytical habits, not an innate trait that separates executives from managers. Moving up requires unlearning the habits that worked one level down.

item.title: Build the Right Thing
item.author: Mike Fisher
item.description: Premature financial validation kills discovery. Early-stage product needs financials as guardrails, not goals, so teams optimize for customer outcomes instead of spreadsheet output.

item.title: The Brag Doc
item.author: Ben Balter
item.description: A weekly five-minute record of impact protects your work from recency bias and review-cycle amnesia. Product-manage your career using shipped outcomes, not memory.

item.title: Sandboxes and Worktrees: My Secure Agentic AI Setup in 2026
item.author: Mike McQuaid
item.description: Stop babysitting one agent at a time. Sandboxes let them run wild safely and git worktrees let them run in parallel, trading more tokens for measurable velocity.

item.title: How Engineering Leaders Calculate AI ROI
item.author: Research-Driven Engineering Leadership
item.description: AI amplifies the system you already have rather than fixing it. Expect a productivity dip over three months before compounding gains arrive, with realistic first-year ROI around 39%.

item.title: Managing Context in Long-Run Agentic Applications
item.author: Slack Engineering
item.description: Multi-agent systems collapse under accumulated message history. Slack uses structured journals, credibility scoring, and consolidated timelines to keep coherence across hundreds of requests without passing raw history forward.

item.title: The Shift to Managing Managers
item.author: Kevin Goldsmith
item.description: Hands-on managers who keep solving problems directly stall the layer below them. The lever shifts to enabling other managers through shared context, multiplying impact precisely when you step away.

item.title: Rift
item.author: Christopher Meiklejohn
item.description: Thirty years of writing code with Phish on dissolved when managing agents replaced hands-on work. The trade buys leverage but surfaces a harder question: where does flow live in a queue-driven workflow?

item.title: Managing a Team That Didn't Choose You
item.author: Anton Zaides
item.description: The 30-60-90 onboarding plan breaks on inherited teams. Reading context first, fractured morale, structural gaps, unmet needs, beats imposing a template that ignores what's already there.

item.title: How React Streams UI Out of Order
item.author: Sankalpa Acharya
item.description: React decouples delivery from completion. Fast components ship immediately with placeholder markers while slow resolvers fill in asynchronously, turning streaming into a composition primitive.

item.title: 10 Lessons for Agentic Coding
item.author: Drew Breunig
item.description: When code is cheap, the moat shifts. Value lives in identifying genuinely hard problems and navigating their complexity, not in automating trivial generation.

item.title: 4 Behaviors That Make You Look Junior
item.author: A Life Engineered
item.description: Visible irritation, emotional bleed, defensive responses, and pessimism erode credibility faster than weak work. Composure under stress is the signal senior looks like from the outside.

item.title: Pushing Local Models With Focus and Polish
item.author: Armin Ronacher
item.description: Local inference fails on fragmentation, not capability. Picking one configuration and treating every failure as a product bug builds confidence faster than chasing breadth across hardware and models.

item.title: Becoming a Business Leader, Not Just a Technical One
item.author: Kevin Goldsmith
item.description: Senior engineers plateau at the business fluency ceiling, not the technical one. Translating technical choices into revenue impact and customer consequence is the work that earns a seat at the table.

item.title: Why Engineering Teams Swing Between Process Extremes
item.author: Incremental Forgetting
item.description: Trade-offs are permanent, not solvable, so teams oscillate instead of settling. Healthier course corrections come from watching direction of movement, not chasing the next opposite.

item.title: Projecting React
item.author: Tanner Linsley
item.description: React's API becomes a specification, not the implementation. An AI-generated lightweight variant lands ~9KB client and 2-3x faster SSR by treating the API surface as a target rather than a source.

item.title: Accessibility in React: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
item.author: Certificates.dev
item.description: Semantic HTML, proper labels, focus management in SPAs, and live regions cover most accessibility failures. Native elements do the work for free.

item.title: Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox
item.author: Mozilla Hacks
item.description: AI-powered bug hunting surfaced 271 Firefox vulnerabilities by steering agents to generate and validate hypotheses. Models finally got capable enough to separate signal from slop.

item.title: Why Can't They Just? Revisited
item.author: Lara Hogan
item.description: Frustration masks incomplete context. Leaders shift the question toward collaborative problem-solving, acknowledging real constraints while identifying where influence actually exists.

item.title: Local AI Needs to Be the Norm
item.author: unix.foo
item.description: On-device AI eliminates vendor dependencies, privacy baggage, and network fragility. You build trust by not needing a privacy policy in the first place.

item.title: Sometimes Your Job is to Get in the Way
item.author: Rands
item.description: Effective leadership demands knowing when to step back and when to decisively intervene. The discipline is not picking a stance, it is recognizing which moment you are in.

item.title: The AI Coding Agent Manifesto
item.author: Wix Engineering
item.description: Generation speed is no longer the bottleneck. Production-grade agent work shifts focus to verification, explicit contracts, and architectural clarity the agent can actually execute.

item.title: What's In It For Me Architecture
item.author: Frederick Vanbrabant
item.description: Technical excellence alone does not ship. Architects succeed by reading stakeholder motivations and building credibility with decision-makers, not by drawing better diagrams.

item.title: Where Feedback Goes to Die
item.author: BonnyCode
item.description: Feedback turns actionable only when leaders stop judging and start listening. Real change requires earning trust through curiosity, not defending against the signal.

item.title: Why Isn't Everything Different Yet?
item.author: Dave Griffith
item.description: Transformative technology takes decades to reshape society. AI is moving faster than historical norms yet still feels glacial because expectations outpace physics.

item.title: LateOn-Code and ColGrep: Code Retrieval for Agents
item.author: LightOn AI
item.description: LightOn shipped semantic code search models that beat much larger alternatives, plus ColGrep for local hybrid search. Agents find relevant code measurably faster.

item.title: DigitalOcean to Hetzner: $1,432 to $233/month With Zero Downtime
item.author: Ismail Sayeter
item.description: A zero-downtime migration of 248 GB of MySQL, 34 Nginx sites, GitLab, and Neo4j cuts the bill by 84%. Cloud pricing turns inefficient fast once your workload stops being spiky.

item.title: Laws of Software Engineering
item.author: Laws of Software Engineering
item.description: A catalog of principles covering architecture, teams, and decision-making. Read together they reveal that software reflects organizational structure and human constraints more than technology.

item.title: The Critical Shift in What Differentiates Great Leaders
item.author: The Uncommon Executive
item.description: AI commoditizes knowledge and makes raw intellect table stakes. Leaders now differentiate on emotional wisdom, ethical judgment, and creativity, the parts algorithms still miss.

item.title: Do I Belong in Tech Anymore?
item.author: ky.fyi
item.description: AI saturation breeds exhaustion, not from the tools but from unreviewed code and pressure to adopt without consent. The burnout here is grief over the field's abandoned ideals.

item.title: Moving Railway's Frontend Off Next.js
item.author: Railway
item.description: Railway swapped Next.js for Vite plus TanStack Router and cut build times from 10+ minutes to under two. Framework choice matters more than hype when iteration speed is the moat.

item.title: AI Should Elevate Your Thinking, Not Replace It
item.author: Koshy John
item.description: AI removes drudgery, but outsourcing understanding creates a quiet intellectual dependency. Judgment and adaptability stay irreplaceable; tools can only extend them.

item.title: The React Compiler at Eighteen Months
item.author: Sasha Baranov
item.description: Eighteen months in, the compiler auto-memoizes components and retires an entire bug class. Greenfield adoption is smooth; brownfield migrations still surface the rough edges.

item.title: AI's Economics Don't Make Sense
item.author: Ed Zitron
item.description: Subscription pricing has been hiding the real per-token cost of AI products. As billing shifts to usage-based, the unit economics underneath the industry start to unravel.

item.title: Resolve Merge Conflicts the Easy Way
item.author: Phil Haack
item.description: Structural merging via mergiraf plus a Claude Code skill turns conflict resolution into a workflow, not a slog. Tools handle syntax-aware merges so you only weigh in on genuine ambiguity.

item.title: The State of Engineering Management in 2026
item.author: Olczyk
item.description: The middle layer of facilitation roles got squeezed as AI absorbed coordination work. Surviving engineering management demands either deep technical involvement or strategic portfolio leadership.

item.title: Ghostty Is Leaving GitHub
item.author: Mitchell Hashimoto
item.description: A long-time GitHub user moves off the platform after repeated reliability failures in PRs, issues, and Actions. The pain point is the surrounding infrastructure, not git.

item.title: How to Be Direct and Strategic
item.author: The Uncommon Executive
item.description: Directness without strategy is just venting. Reading current beliefs and emotional impact before framing your message is what makes the same words actually land.

item.title: A Product Manager's Guide to Painted-Door Tests
item.author: C.R. Stanier
item.description: Painted-door tests gauge demand without engineering investment by showing fake features and measuring take-rate. A binary signal beats intuition before you commit resources.

item.title: DO_NOT_TRACK: A Privacy Standard for CLIs
item.author: DO_NOT_TRACK
item.description: One environment variable replaces a patchwork of per-tool telemetry opt-outs. A single standard for CLI and TUI tools to respect user intent without bespoke flags.

item.title: DeepSeek V4: Frontier Performance at a Fraction of the Price
item.author: Simon Willison
item.description: DeepSeek V4-Pro and V4-Flash hit competitive frontier performance while undercutting price dramatically. Flash undercuts GPT-5.4 Nano, Pro undercuts every flagship.

item.title: Finding Comfort in the Uncertainty
item.author: Annie Vella
item.description: Forty of the sharpest minds in software gathered to map the AI-shaped future. The biggest takeaway. Nobody has it figured out, and that shared uncertainty is oddly the most useful answer.

item.title: What I Learned From Nearly 1,000 Interviews at Amazon
item.author: A Life Engineered
item.description: A decade as an Amazon Bar Raiser, distilled into what actually separates strong candidates from the rest. Signal beats polish, and most interviewers look for the wrong things.

item.title: Evaluating GenAI Features in Enterprise Software Requires a Human Touch
item.author: Mario Barrena
item.description: Automated benchmarks miss what actually matters in enterprise GenAI. Real quality signals come from humans in the loop, not leaderboards.

item.title: The Uphill Climb of Making Diff Lines Performant
item.author: GitHub Engineering
item.description: GitHub rebuilt diff rendering and found the win was not smarter code but less of it. The fastest path to performance often runs through simplicity.

item.title: The Center Has a Bias
item.author: Armin Ronacher
item.description: The middle ground on AI isn't neutral. It's occupied by people who actually used the tools long enough to judge them. Non-use is not the same as balance.

item.title: AI Cybersecurity After Mythos: The Jagged Frontier
item.author: Stanislav Fort
item.description: Cybersecurity capability in LLMs is jagged. It does not scale smoothly with size, generation, or price. Small open-weights models matched a flagship on the same FreeBSD exploit at a fraction of the cost.

item.title: The Economics of Software Teams
item.author: Viktor Cessan
item.description: A team of eight engineers burns roughly 4,000 euros per working day, yet most organizations have no visibility into that number or what it takes to break even. Two decades of structural blindness now collides with the arrival of LLMs.

item.title: 9 Stupid Power Moves Managers Make
item.author: Yaniv Preiss
item.description: Power moves spring from insecurity, not authority, and they quietly corrode trust. Nine common ones and the damage each leaves behind.

item.title: How Does React Fiber Render Your UI
item.author: Sankalpa Acharya
item.description: Recursive rendering blocks the browser. Fiber slices work into ~5ms chunks so the main thread stays responsive. A walk through the linked-list tree of fiber nodes that powers interruptible reconciliation.

item.title: Signals: The Push-Pull Based Algorithm
item.author: Willy Brauner
item.description: Signals power Solid, Vue, and modern reactivity, yet few devs can explain their internals. Pushes notify downward, pulls re-evaluate upward, and together they keep reactive graphs efficient.

item.title: The Vertical Codebase
item.author: Dominik Dorfmeister
item.description: Organizing code by technical layer scales poorly once features cross boundaries. Slicing vertically by feature keeps related code colocated, reduces cross-cutting churn, and makes ownership obvious.

item.title: Under the Hood of MDN's New Frontend
item.author: Leo McArdle
item.description: MDN rebuilt its frontend and unpacks the why. Lit-powered web components replace a tangle of four git repos, cutting friction for authors of interactive examples.

item.title: Dropping Sprints: A Year with Shape Up
item.author: Anton Zaides
item.description: One year after ditching Scrum for Shape Up, the team moved from maintenance mode to high output with happier engineers. Fixed time with variable scope beat the sprint treadmill.

item.title: Uses for Nested Promises
item.author: James Coglan
item.description: Promise.then() implicitly flattens nested promises, a choice that lost functional programmers the Promises/A+ debate but won on convenience. Real concurrency control code reveals rare but legitimate uses for keeping the nesting intact.

item.title: React Server Components Your Way
item.author: Tanner Linsley
item.description: RSCs became a paradigm you orbit around, not a primitive you reach for. TanStack reframes them as just streams of data the client fetches, caches, and composes. Powerful primitives lose their leverage the moment a framework makes them mandatory.

item.title: Compile-time expressions for TypeScript
item.author: Comptime
item.description: Move computation from runtime to build time. A Vite plugin that evaluates TypeScript expressions at compile time for smaller bundles and better performance.

item.title: Software Engineering at Google: Large-Scale Testing
item.author: Google Engineering
item.description: Google's testing playbook: test size taxonomy, test selection strategies, and how to scale CI/CD without creating brittleness or slow feedback loops.

item.title: Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
item.author: HumanLayer
item.description: Agents reason better with structured context. How to engineer context quality so agents understand code intent and constraints.

item.title: Efficient Design System
item.author: Josh Clark
item.description: Design systems should move slower than the products they serve, yet still enable rapid iteration. How deliberate pace prevents bottlenecks.

item.title: Design System Ecosystem
item.author: Brad Frost
item.description: A mature design system isn't a library, it's an ecosystem. How components, tokens, and governance scale across complex organizations.

item.title: Knowledge Silos: The Engineering Productivity Tax
item.author: Leadership Garden
item.description: Knowledge silos compound every other technical debt. Practical strategies to identify and break them down before they paralyze your team.

item.title: Engineering Metrics Guide
item.author: Refactoring
item.description: Skip the metrics theater. How to design a minimal, effective process that uses the right metrics to drive real improvements in engineering productivity.

item.title: All I Need to Know About Engineering Leadership I Learned From Leave No Trace
item.author: Jacob Kaplan-Moss
item.description: Apply wilderness ethics to engineering leadership: leave systems cleaner than you found them, minimize your footprint, and respect the team's capacity.

item.title: Unexpected Anti-Patterns for Engineering Leaders
item.author: Will Larson
item.description: What looks like a management mistake often works surprisingly well. Larson challenges three conventional anti-patterns that actually drive results at high-performing companies.

item.title: How (some) good corporate engineering blogs are written
item.author: Dan Luu
item.description: Great corporate engineering blogs share specific technical insights rather than abstract principles. They succeed by writing about real problems and trade-offs.

item.title: Technical Debt Financing
item.author: Jack Danger
item.description: Technical debt is a strategic tool for CTOs, not a burden to minimize. When managed intentionally as a financing mechanism, it accelerates delivery without sacrificing velocity.

item.title: Solving staffing challenges with concentric circles
item.author: The Engineering Manager
item.description: Rather than top-down reorganization, solve staffing problems from the inside out using concentric circles to progressively expand and restructure teams.

item.title: Questionable Advice: My boss says we don't need any engineering managers
item.author: Charity Majors
item.description: Navigating a startup culture that rejects management infrastructure. When flat structures work and when they create scaling friction.

item.title: Platform as a Runtime
item.author: InfoQ
item.description: As systems scale, platforms must evolve into managed runtimes that abstract complexity and cognitive load. Moving from passive infrastructure to active runtime enablers.

item.title: Balancing Old Tricks with New Feats: AI-Powered Enzyme to RTL Migration at Slack
item.author: Slack Engineering
item.description: Slack open-sourced their AI-driven migration tool that automatically converts Enzyme tests to React Testing Library, balancing modernization with preservation of testing intent.

item.title: DORA Metrics At Work
item.author: Egor Savochkin
item.description: Booking.com doubled their team's delivery performance in a year by systematically measuring and improving the four DORA metrics.

item.title: Avoiding Skill Atrophy in the Age of AI
item.author: Addy Osmani
item.description: AI coding assistants can accelerate delivery but risk eroding the fundamentals that make engineers effective. Strategies to maintain depth while leveraging AI.

item.title: Design Docs at Google
item.author: Irakli Nadareishvili
item.description: Design docs are a cornerstone of Google's engineering culture, serving as the mechanism for aligning teams and capturing architectural reasoning before code is written.

item.title: Catching Compromised Cookies
item.author: Slack Engineering
item.description: Cookies are ubiquitous client-side state flowing across every request, making them a critical security surface. How Slack detects and mitigates compromised session cookies.

item.title: Shipping incrementally
item.author: Zahra Jabeen
item.description: Continuous incremental shipping beats ambitious batches. Regular releases reduce risk, gather feedback faster, and keep momentum strong.

item.title: Leading while learning
item.author: Bence A. Toth
item.description: Effective leadership isn't about having all answers. Create psychological safety where learning is expected, failure is normalized, and your team drives innovation.

item.title: Leadership Strategies for Product Maturity Phases
item.author: Abdul A. Popoola
item.description: Engineering challenges shift as products mature. Startup hustle, scaleup organization, and enterprise reliability each demand different strategies.

item.title: How Airbnb Smoothly Upgrades React
item.author: Airbnb Engineering
item.description: Incremental infrastructure modernization avoids the risk of full rewrites. Airbnb's approach to rolling out new React features while maintaining stability.

item.title: It's Time to Be the Bad Guy
item.author: Anna J McDougall
item.description: Strong engineering managers protect their teams by absorbing difficult decisions. Taking ownership means sometimes being the one who makes unpopular calls.

item.title: Context Engineering: Bringing Engineering Discipline to Prompts
item.author: Addy Osmani
item.description: Effective AI prompting requires the same information architecture rigor we apply to software. Structure context intentionally for consistently better outputs.

item.title: Building stronger engineering teams with aligned autonomy
item.author: Stack Overflow
item.description: Teams perform best when individual autonomy aligns with shared goals. Give engineers clear direction and freedom to solve problems their way.

item.title: Leadership co-processing with LLMs
item.author: The Engineering Manager
item.description: LLMs can be powerful thinking partners for engineering leaders. Using them creatively for brainstorming and decision analysis sharpens your leadership.

item.title: The reality of AI-Assisted software engineering productivity
item.author: Addy Osmani
item.description: What the data really shows about AI coding tools in 2025. Most effective as assistants handling boilerplate, not as replacements for human judgment.

item.title: Why LLMs Can't Really Build Software
item.author: Zed
item.description: Writing code is only one part of effective software engineering. LLMs excel at code generation but lack the architectural thinking and quality assurance that define professional development.

item.title: Going direct
item.author: The Engineering Manager
item.description: Effective organizations communicate fluidly across org chart boundaries rather than rigidly following reporting lines, accelerating decision-making.

item.title: How to Use Claude Code Subagents to Parallelize Development
item.author: Zach Wills
item.description: Lessons from building a metrics tool using subagents to split work in parallel, demonstrating concrete patterns for AI-accelerated development workflows.

item.title: Just Talk To It
item.author: Peter Steinberger
item.description: A grounded, practical approach to working with AI coding agents that cuts through hype and focuses on what actually works.

item.title: BFCM Readiness 2025
item.author: Shopify Engineering
item.description: Technical strategies and infrastructure patterns for handling peak traffic during Black Friday and Cyber Monday at scale.

item.title: Introducing advanced tool use
item.author: Anthropic
item.description: Claude can now discover and dynamically execute tools in real-time, enabling AI agents to take actions directly in external systems without pre-integration.

item.title: 'Good engineering management' is a fad
item.author: Will Larson
item.description: Challenges the assumption that modern management practices are universally correct, arguing context and organizational needs matter more than dogma.

item.title: 21 Lessons from 14 Years at Google
item.author: Addy Osmani
item.description: Distilled wisdom on code quality, career progression, and the interpersonal dimensions of engineering drawn from nearly a decade and a half at scale.

item.title: Rise of the 'operator EM'
item.author: One to N
item.description: The playbook for engineering management has shifted in the post-ZIRP era, requiring managers to balance efficiency with the realities of constrained resources.

item.title: Useful engineering management artifacts
item.author: Bjorn Roche
item.description: Document templates and structural tools that help scaling engineering organizations maintain clarity and alignment as teams grow.

item.title: Building High-Performing Remote Engineering Teams
item.author: Hans Reinl
item.description: Explores the distinct challenges and opportunities of leading engineering teams across distributed locations, moving beyond one-size-fits-all remote work policies.

item.title: One bottleneck at a time
item.author: The Engineering Manager
item.description: Manager instinct often says fix everything at once, but the easy way forward is paradoxically harder. Tackle bottlenecks sequentially to avoid chaos.

item.title: The Next Two Years of Software Engineering
item.author: Addy Osmani
item.description: Five critical questions are reshaping how we build software. Competing scenarios for each and what they mean for your choices today.

item.title: The Architect's Guide to Micro-Frontends
item.author: Developers Voice
item.description: Scale frontend architecture without scaling complexity. Module Federation enables independent teams to ship in parallel without coordination overhead.

item.title: Conflict Between Neurotypes
item.author: Isaac Z. Schlueter
item.description: Neurodiversity isn't just about accommodation. It's about understanding how different thinking styles create friction in teams and how to navigate it.

item.title: Aligning Product and GTM with Customer Value Metrics
item.author: Dan Teodosiu and Dave Kellogg
